title: What Actually Changed in Home Service Lead Generation
content:
###  **More Competition for the Same Attention** 

The number of home service companies competing for a given suburb has grown, while the number of homeowners in it has not. Every channel now carries more brands chasing the same households. 

###  **Homeowners Are Better at Filtering** 

Unread mail. Unopened email. Unanswered calls from unknown numbers. Door hangers removed and discarded without a glance. None of this reflects a lack of interest in home services — it reflects a learned defense against volume. 

### **Paid Channels Got More Expensive Without Getting Better** 

Cost per lead has climbed across most paid home service categories. That is the auction working as designed. It also means a channel that was comfortably profitable a few years ago may now be marginal at the same conversion rate. 

###  **What Still Works** 

Direct human conversation is the one channel that has not degraded the same way, for a straightforward reason: it cannot be filtered in advance. A homeowner may decline it, but they engage with it before deciding, which is more than can be said for most of what arrives at their house. 

###  **The Practical Conclusion** 

None of this argues for abandoning digital or paid channels. It argues for not depending on them alone, and for keeping at least one channel that does not rely on getting past a filter.
